research_rationale:
EO 7308 (February 28, 1936, Franklin D. Roosevelt). Text and identity: read in full in the registered American Presidency Project transcription (jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts; grade mirror_transcription, acceptable_as_original false; standing note: original not yet held). Page check per jobs/claim-kit/AGENT_PROTOCOL.md (working-text paragraph), done 2026-10-28: the APP page record with the same sha256 in jobs/app-executive-orders/output/MIRROR_DOCUMENTS.jsonl has a heading naming EO 7308, its date (February 28, 1936) appears in the held text, and its text_sha256 equals the held file's. Clauses are quoted from that registered file, not from the unregistered clause-drafts copy. It exempts Carl F. Jeansen, principal engineer (Ordnance), Bureau of Ordnance, Navy Department from section 204 of the Economy Act of June 30, 1932 and continues the employee in the service until April 1, 1937. It recites that Jeansen was exempted for one year by EO 6914 of December 6, 1934 and 'further' exempts him. Identity: number, date, person and end date agree across the APP page, the census register and the WPA 1944 numbered list. Legal reading: a single time-limited grant that ends by its own terms on 1937-04-01, inclusive. Later orders naming it, recorded as later events with their own dates and quotes: EO 7569 (March 3, 1937) recites EO 6914 and EO 7308 ('periods totaling two years') and further exempts Jeansen until April 1, 1938. Each recites this order as past history and grants a new period; none revokes or amends this order, so none is this order's end. Searches made on 2026-10-28: (1) census titles in jobs/domesday-register/output/REGISTER.csv with retirement wording for the surname; (2) every WPA 1944 numbered-list entry (jobs/x1-class-engine/data/WPA_NUMBERED_ENTRIES.csv, whitespace-insensitive) for the surname with retirement wording; (3) a full-text search of every held order text under jobs/*/output/texts and jobs/*/data for the person's full name within reach of 'retire' or 'exempt'; (4) a citation search of every held order text for 'Order No. 7308' and list forms ('Orders Nos. ... 7308'). They found this order and the later orders recorded as later events, and nothing else naming this employee; the earlier order it recites is part of the employee's history, not a later event. Authority: section 204 of Part II of the Legislative Appropriation Act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), whose proviso lets the President exempt a person from automatic separation at retirement age. No held source shows section 204 repealed or amended before this order's stated end. Held texts of later exemptions show the President still granting exemptions under section 204 through and after this date (EO 7725 of October 12, 1937, running to November 1, 1938, and EO 7842 of March 15, 1938, running to June 1, 1939), which corroborates that the statutory scheme ran through the stated date.
